review_planner.summary: Review plan for string nodes integration

tasks.title: Validate StringConcatenate and StringSubstring handle None/empty inputs
tasks.description: Verify that StringConcatenate.execute and StringSubstring.execute handle None inputs and empty strings gracefully without raising exceptions. Check if string concatenation and slicing behave correctly when either operand is None or empty.

tasks.title: Review RegexMatch and RegexExtract error handling for invalid regex patterns
tasks.description: Verify that RegexMatch.execute and RegexExtract.execute properly catch and handle re.error exceptions for malformed regex patterns. Confirm that the default behavior (returning False or empty string) is correct and doesn't silently fail or crash.

tasks.title: Verify StringSubstring bounds checking for start/end indices
tasks.description: Check if StringSubstring.execute validates that start and end parameters are within reasonable bounds or handles out-of-range indices gracefully. Python slicing is forgiving, but verify there's no unintended behavior with negative indices or extremely large values.

tasks.title: Confirm nodes_string.py registration in nodes.py init_builtin_extra_nodes
tasks.description: Verify that nodes_string.py is properly registered in the nodes.py file's init_builtin_extra_nodes function and is loaded without import errors. Check for any missing dependencies or circular import risks.

tasks.title: Review StringReplace behavior for overlapping or empty find/replace strings
tasks.description: Test or verify that StringReplace.execute handles edge cases such as empty find strings, empty replace strings, or overlapping patterns correctly without unexpected behavior.

tasks.title: Verify RegexExtract group_index parameter bounds and defaults
tasks.description: Check if RegexExtract.execute validates that group_index is within valid bounds for the given regex pattern. The UI shows min=0, max=100, but verify runtime handling when group_index exceeds actual groups in the pattern.

tasks.title: Review case_insensitive and case_sensitive parameters in StringCompare and StringContains
tasks.description: Verify that case_insensitive and case_sensitive parameters work correctly for all modes in StringCompare and StringContains. Ensure the case handling logic doesn't introduce unexpected behavior with mixed case strings or special characters.

1.summary:
The diff shows a new file `comfy_extras/nodes_string.py` with multiple string utility classes. The task specifically asks to validate `StringConcatenate` and `StringSubstring` handle None/empty inputs. Examining the code:

1. `StringConcatenate.execute` (lines 16-18): `return string_a + string_b,` - No None checking. If either input is None, `None + string` will raise TypeError.

2. `StringSubstring.execute` (lines 37-39): `return string[start:end],` - No None checking. If `string` is None, slicing will raise TypeError. Also no validation of start/end as valid integers.

3. Other classes in the file (StringLength, CaseConverter, etc.) also have similar issues, but the task focuses on StringConcatenate and StringSubstring.

4. The file is new (lines 1-322), so there are no tests covering these edge cases.

I should create findings for the two specific classes mentioned in the task, with proper severity ratings and actionable recommendations.

Context does not show input validation behavior from the node system itself - whether IO.STRING prevents None at a higher level is unknown.

3.summary: The diff shows a new node StringSubstring in comfy_extras/nodes_string.py that performs string slicing with user-provided start and end parameters. Python slicing handles out-of-bounds and negative indices gracefully by clamping values (e.g., string[1000:2000] on a 10-char string returns ''), but the node does not validate or warn about these behaviors. This could lead to silent incorrect outputs that confuse users or mask bugs in workflows. There is no security risk (no injection/DoS), but it's a usability/robustness issue. I'll create one candidate finding for this logic/UX problem.

def execute(self, string_a, string_b, **kwargs):
        return string_a + string_b,
candidate_findings.failure_mode: TypeError when either string_a or string_b is None. Python's + operator does not support concatenation with None values, causing the node to crash instead of handling gracefully.

"""Comfy-specific type hinting"""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Literal, TypedDict, Optional
from typing_extensions import NotRequired
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from enum import Enum


class StrEnum(str, Enum):
    """Base class for string enums. Python's StrEnum is not available until 3.11."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.value


class IO(StrEnum):
    """Node input/output data types.

    Includes functionality for ``"*"`` (`ANY`) and ``"MULTI,TYPES"``.
    """

    STRING = "STRING"
    IMAGE = "IMAGE"
    MASK = "MASK"
    LATENT = "LATENT"
    BOOLEAN = "BOOLEAN"
    INT = "INT"
    FLOAT = "FLOAT"
    COMBO = "COMBO"
    CONDITIONING = "CONDITIONING"
    SAMPLER = "SAMPLER"
    SIGMAS = "SIGMAS"
    GUIDER = "GUIDER"
    NOISE = "NOISE"
    CLIP = "CLIP"
    CONTROL_NET = "CONTROL_NET"
    VAE = "VAE"
    MODEL = "MODEL"
    CLIP_VISION = "CLIP_VISION"
    CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT = "CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT"
    STYLE_MODEL = "STYLE_MODEL"
    GLIGEN = "GLIGEN"
    UPSCALE_MODEL = "UPSCALE_MODEL"
    AUDIO = "AUDIO"
    WEBCAM = "WEBCAM"
    POINT = "POINT"
    FACE_ANALYSIS = "FACE_ANALYSIS"
    BBOX = "BBOX"
    SEGS = "SEGS"
    VIDEO = "VIDEO"

    ANY = "*"
    """Always matches any type, but at a price.

    Causes some functionality issues (e.g. reroutes, link types), and should be avoided whenever possible.
    """
    NUMBER = "FLOAT,INT"
    """A float or an int - could be either"""
    PRIMITIVE = "STRING,FLOAT,INT,BOOLEAN"
    """Could be any of: string, float, int, or bool"""

    def __ne__(self, value: object) -> bool:
        if self == "*" or value == "*":
            return False
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            return True
        a = frozenset(self.split(","))
        b = frozenset(value.split(","))
        return not (b.issubset(a) or a.issubset(b))


class RemoteInputOptions(TypedDict):
    route: str
    """The route to the remote source."""
    refresh_button: bool
    """Specifies whether to show a refresh button in the UI below the widget."""
    control_after_refresh: Literal["first", "last"]
    """Specifies the control after the refresh button is clicked. If "first", the first item will be automatically selected, and so on."""
    timeout: int
    """The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the remote source in milliseconds."""
    max_retries: int
    """The maximum number of retries before aborting the request."""
    refresh: int
    """The TTL of the remote input's value in milliseconds. Specifies the interval at which the remote input's value is refreshed."""


class MultiSelectOptions(TypedDict):
    placeholder: NotRequired[str]
    """The placeholder text to display in the multi-select widget when no items are selected."""
    chip: NotRequired[bool]
    """Specifies whether to use chips instead of comma separated values for the multi-select widget."""


class InputTypeOptions(TypedDict):
    """Provides type hinting for the return type of the INPUT_TYPES node function.

    Due to IDE limitations with unions, for now all options are available for all types (e.g. `label_on` is hinted even when the type is not `IO.BOOLEAN`).

    Comfy Docs: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/backend/datatypes
    """

    default: NotRequired[bool | str | float | int | list | tuple]
    """The default value of the widget"""
    defaultInput: NotRequired[bool]
    """@deprecated in v1.16 frontend. v1.16 frontend allows input socket and widget to co-exist.
    - defaultInput on required inputs should be dropped.
    - defaultInput on optional inputs should be replaced with forceInput.
    Ref: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/pull/3364
    """
    forceInput: NotRequired[bool]
    """Forces the input to be an input slot rather than a widget even a widget is available for the input type."""
    lazy: NotRequired[bool]
    """Declares that this input uses lazy evaluation"""
    rawLink: NotRequired[bool]
    """When a link exists, rather than receiving the evaluated value, you will receive the link (i.e. `["nodeId", <outputIndex>]`). Designed for node expansion."""
    tooltip: NotRequired[str]
    """Tooltip for the input (or widget), shown on pointer hover"""
    socketless: NotRequired[bool]
    """All inputs (including widgets) have an input socket to connect links. When ``true``, if there is a widget for this input, no socket will be created.
    Available from frontend v1.17.5
    Ref: https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/pull/3548
    """
    widgetType: NotRequired[str]
    """Specifies a type to be used for widget initialization if different from the input type.
    Available from frontend v1.18.0
    https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/pull/3550"""
    # class InputTypeNumber(InputTypeOptions):
    # default: float | int
    min: NotRequired[float]
    """The minimum value of a number (``FLOAT`` | ``INT``)"""
    max: NotRequired[float]
    """The maximum value of a number (``FLOAT`` | ``INT``)"""
    step: NotRequired[float]
    """The amount to increment or decrement a widget by when stepping up/down (``FLOAT`` | ``INT``)"""

class CheckLazyMixin:
    """Provides a basic check_lazy_status implementation and type hinting for nodes that use lazy inputs."""

    def check_lazy_status(self, **kwargs) -> list[str]:
        """Returns a list of input names that should be evaluated.

        This basic mixin impl. requires all inputs.

        :kwargs: All node inputs will be included here.  If the input is ``None``, it should be assumed that it has not yet been evaluated.  \
            When using ``INPUT_IS_LIST = True``, unevaluated will instead be ``(None,)``.

        Params should match the nodes execution ``FUNCTION`` (self, and all inputs by name).
        Will be executed repeatedly until it returns an empty list, or all requested items were already evaluated (and sent as params).

        Comfy Docs: https://docs.comfy.org/custom-nodes/backend/lazy_evaluation#defining-check-lazy-status
        """

        need = [name for name in kwargs if kwargs[name] is None]
        return need

class StrEnum(str, Enum):

    def __str__(self) -> str:

    """Node input/output data types.

    Includes functionality for ``"*"`` (`ANY`) and ``"MULTI,TYPES"``.
    """

    STRING = "STRING"
    IMAGE = "IMAGE"
    MASK = "MASK"
    LATENT = "LATENT"
    BOOLEAN = "BOOLEAN"

    COMBO = "COMBO"

    SIGMAS = "SIGMAS"
    GUIDER = "GUIDER"
    NOISE = "NOISE"
    CLIP = "CLIP"
    CONTROL_NET = "CONTROL_NET"
    VAE = "VAE"
    MODEL = "MODEL"
    CLIP_VISION = "CLIP_VISION"
    CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT = "CLIP_VISION_OUTPUT"
    STYLE_MODEL = "STYLE_MODEL"
    GLIGEN = "GLIGEN"
    UPSCALE_MODEL = "UPSCALE_MODEL"
    AUDIO = "AUDIO"
    WEBCAM = "WEBCAM"
    POINT = "POINT"
    FACE_ANALYSIS = "FACE_ANALYSIS"
    BBOX = "BBOX"
    SEGS = "SEGS"
    VIDEO = "VIDEO"

    ANY = "*"
    """Always matches any type, but at a price.

    Causes some functionality issues (e.g. reroutes, link types), and should be avoided whenever possible.
    """
    NUMBER = "FLOAT,INT"
    """A float or an int - could be either"""
    PRIMITIVE = "STRING,FLOAT,INT,BOOLEAN"
    """Could be any of: string, float, int, or bool"""

    def __ne__(self, value: object) -> bool:
        if self == "*" or value == "*":
            return False
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            return True
        a = frozenset(self.split(","))
        b = frozenset(value.split(","))
        return not (b.issubset(a) or a.issubset(b))
